items.subject: Grocery: semantic sweep found 7 product(s) no rule can see - 2026-09-18 (resumed; 8 on 2026-09-20)
evidence: RE-MEASURED FIRST, AND THE TWO BLOCKING FAULTS ARE NOT WHAT THE PLAN CALLED THEM. plan-2026-09-20-4 recorded them as '2 pre-existing feminine-pads PRICE-DRIFT faults'. Read off out/tile-integrity.json at 16:47 they are: feminine-pads [Sam's Club] 'board $0.1683 vs link $0.1357 (24.1% off)' and feminine-pads [Fareway] 'board $0.2081 vs link $0.1942 (7.2% off)', BOTH with board name == link name. Neither is a wrong product and neither is a reader-facing lie about which product the tile opens: what is stale is OUR RECORD of the link's price, which is the only thing audit-tile-integrity can compare.

FAREWAY, AND THE BOARD IS RIGHT. The row carries ad_price $6.99 AND regular $7.49. sale-windows.json window 275 records the $6.99 as a sale with sale_start 2026-09-14, sale_end 2026-09-19, refresh_on 2026-09-20, so on 2026-09-20 the cell correctly fell back to the store's own posted everyday price, $7.49 / 36 ct = 0.2081. The stored link still carried 6.99, derived while the sale was running. Every Fareway capture from 2026-07-23 to 2026-09-20 carries the same pair, so this is not a capture gap.

SAM'S CLUB, AND THE BOARD IS RIGHT THERE TOO. Board $15.48 / 92 ct = 0.1683, as_of 2026-09-19, corroborated by the EXTERNAL REFERENT on the same row: Sam's own published sams_unit_price '$0.17/ea'. The stored link carried $12.48, which is the price in sams-deals-2026-08-15.json and sams-deals-2026-07-29.json, and it was stamped 'verified: 2026-09-19 DERIVED from the price row (same record the board priced)'. That stamp is false, and how it got written is the defect.

THE MECHANISM, PROVEN IN THE SOURCE. derive-links-from-prices.ps1 decided an entry needed no work with `if ($cur -and ([string]$cur.url) -eq $url) { $already++; continue }` - the URL alone. The URL is the identity; the price is the fact; only the identity was ever compared. So a store repricing the SAME product page, or a sale expiring, left the snapshot untouched forever. That is Fareway. And the entry it WRITES took its price from $r.ad_price, so even a forced rewrite would have re-written 6.99 against a board publishing 7.49.

AND THE SAM'S HALF IS AN UNANNOUNCED SOURCE CHANGE. All 2,802 rows in sams-deals-2026-09-19.json carry an ALPHANUMERIC sams_item_id ('4YKF09SXNTK8'); Get-RowUrl builds a Sam's URL only from '^\d+$', because bare /ip/<numeric> is the only shape this estate has proven. So the fresh row was rejected as having no identity, and the index's 'a row carrying identity beats one that does not' fallback substituted the 2026-07-29 row - carrying its July price - and the writer then stamped today's date on it. That is the two-pipeline bug this script exists to kill, reappearing inside the script.

THE WIDENING, RE-RUN LIVE AND ACCEPTED. With both faults healed, apply-coverage-batch.ps1 over the same three patterns: 'crown changes: 0'; feminine-pads 6 -> 6, maple-syrup 5 -> 5, onion-soup-mix 3 -> 3; 'value: +0 cell(s), -0 cell(s)'; reveals 2, 3 and 2; 'theft check: OK'; then 'tile-integrity failed: 0 hard fault(s) on BATCH commodities, 198 pre-existing elsewhere' and 'BATCH ACCEPTED'. Every number reproduces plan-2026-09-20-4.routing.json exactly, so the contract was diffed and not rebuilt.

THE LINK LAYER, BEFORE AND AFTER, ON ONE BOARD. audit-tile-integrity over comparison-2026-09-20: PRICE-DRIFT 225 -> 198 (Fareway 26 -> 0), NO-LINK 225 -> 219, ACCURACY 0 of 2,410 linked tiles both times, exit 0 with TILE-INTEGRITY-COMPLETE. A global dry run of the fixed script reports 144 further refreshable entries and 82 it refuses (Sam's Club 81, Baker's 1).

THE SWEEP ITSELF, RE-RUN AFTER THE WIDENING LANDED. audit-semantic-identity.ps1 exit 0, SEMANTIC-IDENTITY-COMPLETE: 'examined 2629 shipped pair(s) and 8669 rule-invisible product(s) in 1.5s on cuda' and 'COVERAGE (real products no rule can see): 0 product(s) across 0 commodit(y/ies)'. This morning's file (out/semantic-findings.json, 15:59) carried 8 across 6 commodities: wild-rice 1, laundry-detergent 1, cooked-jasmine-rice 2 (ruled on 2026-09-19) and maple-syrup 1, onion-soup-mix 1, feminine-pads 2 (admitted by the three patterns shipped today). 8 -> 0, which is what closes 2026-09-19-4f01f6 as well.

items.root_cause: CARRIED FORWARD VERBATIM from plan-2026-09-18.json item 2026-09-18-37ac63: the sweep's alert cannot tell 'no include matches' from 'an exclude refused it', so every product a rule correctly refuses is re-paged as invisible; and the only suppressor it honours is a per-name ruling, which a store defeats by listing the next SKU (4-count after 12-count) and which the -File comma trap can silently turn into a ruling that matches nothing. WHAT BLOCKED THE REMEDY, one level down and found today: the link record that audit-tile-integrity grades is written by derive-links-from-prices, which treated URL equality as proof the whole record was current, and took its price from the row's ad_price rather than from the price the board actually published - so a repriced page and an expired sale both left a snapshot the audit correctly flagged and the script structurally could not repair.

root_fix.what: make the link record mean what the script's own header claims - one record, so the price and its link cannot drift apart - by comparing the FACT and not only the identity, and by writing only a price that both the board published and the row observed
root_fix.exact_change: (1) `already` now requires same URL AND Test-EntryStale false, graded through the same pu-lib Get-LinkPerUnit and the same 2% / half-cent bar audit-tile-integrity uses, everyday cells only. (2) the written price is the board cell's own published price, accepted only after it is proved equal (to half a cent) to the row's ad_price or its regular; otherwise NO link is written and the refusal is COUNTED and named per store ('board price not observed on the row: 82, Sam's Club 81'). (3) -ProductUrlsFile and -SelfTest added so the write rules can be driven on frozen fixtures instead of the live link layer.

items.leaves_open: TWO, both measured. (a) 198 tiles still record a price the board no longer publishes: 144 of them the fixed script can refresh store by store, and 81 Sam's Club cells it structurally cannot, because all 2,802 rows of the current capture carry an alphanumeric sams_item_id and no Sam's URL shape but bare /ip/<numeric> has been proven here. (b) clause 2 of the root cause is untouched: known-wrong is keyed on commodity|store|normalised NAME, so the next SKU of an already-adjudicated shape pages again - it fired 3 times on 2026-09-20 (two Ben's Original Ready Rice flavour SKUs, one Stayfree SKU).

prevention.what: the producer of the link record stops asserting freshness it has not checked: an entry is refreshed when the FACT moved, not only when the identity did, and a price the row never observed is refused and counted instead of being taken from whichever older row happened to carry a linkable id. Upstream of that, the emitting check classifies every finding with explain-coverage-gap's own classifier before it pages, so only genuinely rule-invisible products reach a human.
prevention.exact_change: derive-links-from-prices.ps1: the `already` short-circuit gains Test-EntryStale (same lib, same bar as the grading audit); the written price becomes the board's published price proved against the row's own ad_price or regular, with a per-store counter for every refusal; -ProductUrlsFile and -SelfTest make both rules testable. The classifier and the -File comma guard shipped 2026-09-18 and were verified working again today (13 EXCLUDED + 1 truncation suppressed of 22 on 2026-09-20).

items.subject: Board verification: defect rate 37.1% is above the last measured 18.2%
evidence: THE CLASS FIX IS IN THE CODE AND I RAN IT. record-sample-verdict.ps1 now records a rubric per run (the sha256 of the BODY of its notes' 'Adjudication standard' section, plus version and counted subclasses) and compares two whole-board rates ONLY when both runs carry the same rules_sha.

VERIFIED LIVE ON THE TWO RUNS THAT CAUSED THIS ALERT. 'powershell -File grocery\record-sample-verdict.ps1 -Report -CompareLast' exits 0 and prints: 'RATE-VS-LAST verdict=rubric-changed why=not-recorded scope=whole-board new=2026-09-17 37.1% ... last=2026-08-15 18.2% ... like_for_like=not-computable (the last run recorded no rubric, so which subclasses it counted is unknown) intervals=overlap new_rubric=none last_rubric=none (measured under different rules: the two whole-board rates are NOT compared)'. Before the fix this same pair produced the subject 'defect rate 37.1% is above the last measured 18.2%'.

IT FAILS CLOSED, WHICH IS THE HARDER HALF. Both runs pre-date rubric recording, so the verdict is 'not-recorded' rather than 'differs', and the restricted like-for-like rate is declared not computable rather than guessed. An unknown is reported as an unknown.

AND IT IS FIXTURED. The suite carries the case headed 'a rate is compared only with a rate adjudicated under the same rubric (2026-09-19, queue 641ec6)', with fixture runs that differ in rules_sha and in which subclasses they counted.

RESIDUAL OWNERSHIP CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. open_questions_for_brad.question: CARRIED FORWARD from plan-2026-09-20-4.json, unchanged and still unanswered. known-wrong is keyed on commodity|store|normalised NAME, so every new SKU of an already-adjudicated shape pages again. 37ac63 recorded this at 0 occurrences on 2026-09-18; it fired 3 times on 2026-09-20 (two Ben's Original Ready Rice flavour SKUs, one Stayfree SKU). Should a ruling be able to name a SHAPE rather than a name, and if so what stops a shape-keyed ruling from silently suppressing a product nobody adjudicated? Nobody has measured what a pattern-keyed known-wrong entry would suppress across the 326 existing rulings, and this lane will not invent that.

CARRIED FORWARD from plan-2026-09-20-2.json. cost-recipes orders the price bases board, then feed, then hand-typed LABEL, then the carriage ledger. five-spice-powder therefore prices from a 2026-07-18 Walmart label at $8.13 per 1.75 oz while the Hy-Vee carriage ledger - a live in-store read of price, size, product id and date - says $9.99, a 19% understatement on 7 live recipes. Should a carriage-ledger read inside the quarter outrank a hand-typed label price older than it? The money is cents a serving; the principle is which evidence wins when both are real and one is newer. Changing the ordering moves the published per-serving cost of 7 live recipes, so it is a ruling and not an implementation detail.
